answer: Agents periodically post a hashed task output to the ledger; the system keeps a sliding orchard‑sized window of recent hashes and automatically rejects any submission that duplicates a hash within that window. Because each output must incorporate a fresh cedar‑seed from a decentralized beacon, an attacker must expend full compute to generate a distinct result for every Sybil identity each interval, turning the oasis of cheap identities into a costly proof‑of‑unique‑work barrier.
